newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian pension fund assets rise to 1 trln pesos.
newsitem.headline: Colombian pension fund assets rise to 1 trln pesos.

text.p: The total assets of Colombia's private pension funds rose to 1 trillion pesos as of March 31, the last date for which official figures are available, the Banking Superintendency said.

It gave no specific explanation for the increase in assets, which were up from 872 billion pesos in January. But it said steady albeit increasingly slower levels of growth have been seen ever since Colombia established its private pension fund system in 1994.
The system now has 2.1 million affiliates across the country.

A total of nine funds now operate in the country, led by Porvenir, which belongs to industrialist Luis Carlos Sarmiento, Proteccion of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate and Colfondos of the Julio Mario Santo Domingo conglomerate.
A full 24 percent of total assets are administered by Provenir, 21 percent by Proteccion and 17 percent by Colfondos, the Superintendency said.
Colombia's fund assets are relatively small compared to other countries in the region. But they are growing rapidly and some analysts estimate they could reach about $2 billion by early next year.
